title: Default Systems
hook: Whatever your business does when you're not paying attention is what it's actually built to do.
statement: What happens by default ends up running your life and your business.
explainer: Defaults run every day whether you're watching or not. A good one compounds quietly. A bad one compounds just as quietly, in the wrong direction.
sop: Get specific about what your ideal day or outcome looks like.
Score your current Default 1 to 10 against that ideal.
Set up one automation or standing rule that kills a repeat decision.
Take the manual choice away completely.
Review defaults quarterly and automate the next thing you're still deciding.
equation_example: Default is 8, how well your automatic behavior serves you, and Time is 12 months. 8 × 12 = 96. Higher means a strong default is stacking good results without willpower. Lower means a weak one is stacking damage the same way.
question: Write down one default in your week that's working against you and what should replace it.
closing_statement: What you default to is what you actually value.
caption:
Principle Nº 133: Default Systems

Whatever your business does when you're not paying attention is what it's actually built to do.

What happens by default ends up running your life and your business.
